before:
Tidewater Bore Watch — Spring Series Warden Report

Thirty-one wardens covered the lower reach between March and May, most working single-handed on the ebb. Where one warden held a reach alone and could not finish every task before the water turned, bank erosion surveys were logged ahead of bird disturbance counts, and bird disturbance counts ahead of litter tallies. All three stayed within the warden's remit and none was dropped from the schedule; the sequence decided only what survived a short tide. Wardens reported that the arrangement worked well in April and less well in the wet fortnight that followed. The committee has asked that the same three tasks be carried into the autumn series without alteration to who may perform them, or to the forms used.

before:
Bothy Association — Winter Restocking Run, Working Method

The party leaves the road end at first light and works the two lower huts before crossing the burn to the third. Loads are split so that no carrier takes more than fifteen kilos. On arrival the party checks the stove flue, replaces the candle stock, and enters the visit in the book by the door. Walkers who arrive part-way through are told: 'We are very sorry to be in your way; the hut will be clear within the hour, and there is tea going in the meantime.' The party leaves before dusk whatever remains undone, and what is left over is carried to the following weekend.

before:
County Herbarium — Accession Register, Sheet 4471

Sheet 4471 was gathered from the flush above the quarry track in June and mounted the same week. The collector's note gives the altitude as 340 metres and the substrate as flushed mica-schist. On review by the visiting referee the sheet is entered as Carex viridula subsp. brachyrrhyncha, superseding the collector's determination. Fruit measurements and the photograph of the growing site stand as taken, as does the accession number, which stays with the sheet for its lifetime. before:
Burial Ground Committee — Minutes, Item 6: Wall Movement

The clerk reported on the bulge in the north boundary wall, first noticed after the February rain. The mason's letter was read in full. It states that the movement is almost certainly caused by roots of the limes on the neighbouring plot rather than by settlement of the footing. Members asked whether the bulge had grown since midsummer; the clerk said readings would be taken monthly from October against a straightedge kept in the vestry. It was agreed to write to the neighbouring owner, to seek a second opinion before spring, and to defer any decision on rebuilding until both the readings and that opinion are to hand.
after:
Burial Ground Committee — Minutes, Item 6: Wall Movement

The clerk reported on the bulge in the north boundary wall, first noticed after the February rain. The mason's letter was read in full. Members asked whether the bulge had grown since midsummer; the clerk said readings would be taken monthly from October against a straightedge kept in the vestry. It was agreed to write to the neighbouring owner, to seek a second opinion before spring, and to defer any decision on rebuilding until both the readings and that opinion are to hand.

before:
Ferry Slipway Winch — Operator's Manual, Section 3: Cable

The main cable is 24 millimetres in diameter and 118 metres long, of which 96 metres are in service and the remainder is dead turns on the drum. The working length is inspected each Monday for broken wires. The drum brake is tested cold at the start of every shift. Grease points are shown in the diagram overleaf; the two on the fairlead are easily missed. The winch was refitted at the yard at Ardnaig and returned to service in the spring of its fortieth year. Operators should note that the drum turns anticlockwise when the carriage is hauled up the slip, and clockwise when it is eased down.

before:
Small Library — Catalogue Maintenance, Withdrawal Workflow

Withdrawn stock passes through four hands. The volunteer first strikes the item from the shelf list, then removes the pocket and date label, then stamps the title page, and finally moves the item to the sale trolley in the porch. Nothing may be sold that still carries a readable stamp, and the sale price stays at fifty pence for hardbacks and twenty for paperbacks. The shelf list is reconciled against the accession ledger on the last Friday of the month. Volunteers are asked not to withdraw more than thirty items in one session, since the trolley will not hold more and the porch is a fire route.

before:

Contributions for the coming year are worked out for each holding using the Board's 1998 banded acreage table, applied to the area entered at the last survey. This book holds every animal kept in the isolation room. For the purposes of the book, a quarantine day begins at the eight o'clock feed and runs to the same hour the following morning.
